# India fixtures: SYNTHETIC, not market data

Every file in this folder is generated by `make_fixtures.py`. The numbers are
invented. They are shaped exactly like real NSE data (IST session timestamps,
75 five-minute bars a session, rupee prices on a 0.05 tick, Yahoo's chart
payload layout) so the tools can be tested offline, but no price here ever
traded.

Each file carries `"synthetic": true` in its meta, and the test suite asserts
that marker is present, so a synthetic fixture cannot quietly be mistaken for
a capture.

## Why synthetic

The port was written in an environment whose network policy blocks Yahoo,
`nseindia.com` and `api.bseindia.com`, so no real NSE history could be
downloaded. Synthetic data tests the arithmetic, which is what these tests are
for: whether the opening range starts at 09:15, whether square-off fires,
whether costs land on the right leg, whether a stock at its circuit is
skipped. It cannot tell you how a setup actually behaved on NSE.

## Replacing them with real data

The files are in the canonical adapter shape, and the `yahoo-*.json` one is a
raw Yahoo payload, so a real capture is a drop-in replacement with no test
rewrites. On a machine with network access:

```bash
curl -s -A 'Mozilla/5.0' \
  'https://query2.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/RELIANCE.NS?range=60d&interval=5m' \
  > yahoo-RELIANCE-5m.json
```

Then drop `"synthetic": true` from the meta and the guard test will stop
treating it as invented. Tests asserting specific prices will need their
expected values updated to the real ones.

## Files

| file | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| `RELIANCE-5m.json` | 60 full sessions of 5-minute bars, canonical shape |
| `RELIANCE-1m.json` | one session of 1-minute bars (375) |
| `TCS-5m.json` | one session with a clean opening-range breakout |
| `CIRCUITCO-5m.json` | a stock pinned at its upper circuit all day |
| `yahoo-RELIANCE-5m.json` | raw Yahoo chart payload, including null gaps |
